# Operations Risk Monitor

> A multi-agent system that watches operational risk across ocean freight, fuel, labour, weather, and geopolitics, then turns what it finds into briefings you can use - a CLI that produces weekly reports (HTML, Markdown, PDF, PPTX) and a live dashboard that refreshes itself.

The model behind the summaries is yours to choose: everything routes through LiteLLM, so the same code runs on Anthropic, OpenAI, or a local Ollama model. Seven agents each own a slice of risk and share one five-step pipeline (collect, filter, summarize, compose, save). Part of Automatiqa Lab.

## Docs
- [README](https://github.com/automatiqa-lab/risk-monitor/blob/main/README.md): the agents, the harness, setup, and how to run the reports and dashboard
- [COMPLIANCE](https://github.com/automatiqa-lab/risk-monitor/blob/main/COMPLIANCE.md): EU AI Act role classification, Annex III screening, and where the marking sits

## License and provenance

MIT licensed, copyright 2026 Aleks Sidorecs. Upstream model providers are listed in [NOTICE](https://github.com/automatiqa-lab/risk-monitor/blob/main/NOTICE) - the lab does not train or distribute models, and is not a GPAI provider under the EU AI Act.

Output is marked under EU AI Act Article 50. Two kinds of text in a report are model-written: the per-article summaries and the executive briefing. Both carry machine-readable marking under the `automatiqa-disclosure/1` schema - HTML meta tags, Markdown front matter, PDF info dictionary and XMP, PPTX core properties, and an `ai_generated` envelope with an `X-AI-Generated` header on the JSON endpoints. Headlines, dates, figures, source names and links are reproduced unmodified from the sources and are not marked. A report containing no model-written text carries no marking at all, so the absence of an envelope is itself a claim you can rely on. Full reasoning in [COMPLIANCE.md](https://github.com/automatiqa-lab/risk-monitor/blob/main/COMPLIANCE.md).
